chunks: And whoever touches a piece of the body of one devoured by beasts, then ghusl (ritual bath) is upon him if there is a bone in what he touched; but if there is no bone in it, then there is no ghusl upon him for touching it.
And whoever touches a carcass must wash his hands, but ghusl is not upon him; that is only obligatory in the case of the human alone.

And whoever touches a dead person before the ghusl, while the body still retains its warmth, then there is no ghusl upon him. But if he touches him after he becomes cold, then ghusl is upon him. And whoever touches him after he has been washed, then there is no ghusl upon him.

key_terms.أَكِيلِ السَّبُعِ: one whose body has been eaten by beasts
key_terms.الْإِنْسَانِ: the human being, for whom this ruling specifically applies
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath required in specific states of impurity
key_terms.بِحَرَارَتِهِ: while retaining bodily warmth after death
key_terms.عَظْمٌ: bone, whose presence affects the ruling here
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: to be ritually washed after death

ai.seo_question: When does touching a dead body require ghusl in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning touching the dead and parts of a corpse. It distinguishes between human and non-human dead bodies, between the presence or absence of bone, and between touching a deceased person before cooling, after cooling, and after ritual washing.
